file_roles.evidence: Defines the rule that was missing, as an inline body rather than a declaration: 'bool must_avoid_clear_instant_add() const' returns true when the index is instant and any following index is marked to_be_dropped. The comment states the new invariant, 'whether it is forbidden to invoke clear_instant_add()'.

Applies that rule where the metadata was being discarded, 'if (index->table->instant)' becoming 'if (index->table->instant || index->must_avoid_clear_instant_add())', and corrects the metadata-record test from a single 'if (rec_is_alter_metadata(r, *index))' to a branch that first checks '!rec_is_metadata(r, *index)'.
The same guard added to two more conditions that decide whether instant metadata may be cleared, each gaining '&& !cursor->index->must_avoid_clear_instant_add()' or the index-qualified form.

An assertion is weakened and the reason recorded in a disabled comment, '#if 0 /* MDEV-22867 had to relax this */ ... #endif' leaving 'ut_ad(index->is_instant());'. The check had to give way once the metadata is legitimately preserved; it detects nothing about the reported failure.

rationale: The assertion names its site, 'handler0alter.cc:422: void dict_index_t::instant_add_field(const dict_index_t&): Assertion `instant.n_core_fields == n_core_fields' failed', and the test case needs two connections, an ALTER TABLE DROP running against a DELETE that empties the table. The field counts diverge because the instant-ADD metadata was cleared by the emptying path while a NOCOPY drop was still in flight, so the two ends are an ordering between sessions rather than a fault at one site.
